name: NE5532 / NE5532A / SA5532 / SE5532
tagline: The 1979 Signetics dual that became the pro-audio benchmark: 5 nV/√Hz, 600 Ω drive, cheap. Douglas Self's reference.

lineage.note: Introduced the NE5534/NE5532 family; dual version of the NE5534 core. TI SLOS075 keeps the 'NOVEMBER 1979' date.
'Internally-compensated dual low noise operational amplifier' datasheets. Current NXP status unknown.
Now the highest-volume supplier. Moved from SFAB Sherman (150 mm) to RFAB Richardson with a die redesign.
NE5532/D Rev. 1 (Mar 2006), Rev. 2 (Sep 2013); keeps legacy specs. Absorbed Fairchild NE5532/KA5532 in 2016.
Fairchild NE5532 Rev. 1.0.2 (©2009); KA5532 of Samsung origin.
NJM5532 on JRC's own die; reportedly 'looser' sounding.
BA15532, common in Asian consumer gear.

reputation.summary: The reference pro-audio op-amp since 1979 and the stock part rolls are judged against. Douglas Self uses it as his benchmark and blames bad reports on misuse; NwAvGuy's 2011 measurements put it beside far pricier parts. Soomal calls it '号称运放之皇' (reputed king of op-amps); Japan's nabe rates it the baseline audio op-amp. Vintage Signetics/Philips stock has a following.
typical_uses: Mixing consoles and pro line stages into 600 Ω
CD player and DAC I/V and output stages
Preamps, tone controls, active crossovers, powered speakers
Headphone amps, with or without buffers
caveats: New TI die: 5 V/µs, ±18 V max, no 600 Ω specs; ±18–22 V boards have failed QA.
New TI die reportedly drops input diodes and halves HBM ESD (2 kV to 1 kV).
Needs at least about ±5 V; not rail-to-rail. Several mA per package, so it runs warm.
Bipolar bias current causes offset with high source impedance; legacy input diodes rule out comparator use.
Brands differ: Self reportedly found TI noisier than Fairchild/onsemi. Fake 'NOS Signetics/Philips' parts are common.

counterfeit_notes: Remarked fakes are common, especially 'NOS Signetics/Philips' (vintage sells for over 100 RMB in China). Genuine parts draw several mA and drive 600 Ω. New TI parts slew 5 V/µs without input diodes, so neither test proves a fake.

silicon_changes.identification: Part numbers unchanged, no date-code cut-over; 2024+ lots may be new silicon. Legacy parts show anti-parallel diodes between IN+ and IN−; new die reportedly none. Slew 5 vs 9 V/µs.
silicon_changes.summary: TI moved NE5532/A and SA5532/A to an RFAB die (around 2024) shared with LM833, RC4580, MC33078. Rich Cabot: 'they just relabeled a 4580'. The 2023 PCN claimed no impact; SLOS075K followed in Dec 2025 and datasheet PCN 20260429001.1 (first ship 29 Jul 2026). Hackaday (3 Jun 2026) calls it incompatible.

spec_deltas.after: removed (Headphonesty, Mithat, E2E thread); the Rev K description text reportedly still mentions them

spec_deltas.parameter: Equivalent input noise, CMRR, DC AVD

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Full-power bandwidth at 10 V peak falls from about 143 to 80 kHz; 600 Ω drive unguaranteed; ±18–22 V rails overstressed; input clamping gone.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: high: same part number, lower voltage rating, slower slew, halved ESD, no input diodes.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN lists NE5532DR/SA5532ADR (and NE5532AP per E2E 1299478); E2E 1652528 and Hackaday confirmed.

silicon_changes.identification: Pad-printed (tampo) Signetics marking before about 2000, laser-marked Philips parts after.
silicon_changes.summary: Japanese blogs (radiokits.jp, takinx) say later laser-marked Philips parts behave differently at the input diodes and many misbehaved when paired directly. They claim the Signetics masks were lost in the March 2000 Albuquerque fab fire. No vendor document supports this.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Claimed subtle sonic and input-diode differences; anecdotal only.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: no documented spec change; folklore.
silicon_changes.verification: No vendor PCN or datasheet support known.

silicon_changes.vendor: Multiple second sources (TI legacy, onsemi/Fairchild, JRC NJM5532, Signetics/Philips, Raytheon, Rohm, Samsung)
silicon_changes.identification: Manufacturer logo and prefix (NJM, KA, BA, RC), plus the vendor datasheet.
silicon_changes.summary: Each vendor built its own die. Forum reports: Self found TI noisier, with higher HF THD, than Fairchild/onsemi; original Signetics reportedly up to 10 dB quieter and 20 dB lower distortion than modern TI; JRC 'looser'. A Soomal noise gain (JRC5532 to TI5532) is confounded by a crossover retune.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Possible brand differences in noise, HF THD and bias current; evidence mostly forum reports.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: pin- and function-compatible across legacy vendors (post-2024 TI excepted).
silicon_changes.verification: Forum reports kept as stated; not independently checked.

open_questions: When were SLOS075 B, D, E and F issued? Is the cited 'SLOS075L' real? Rev K appears current.
Is there a date-code cutover or marking change (E2E 1294367, NE5532DR symbolization) identifying the new TI die?
Does the new die have PNP or NPN inputs, and are the input diodes really gone?
Confirm Rev K figures (6/16 mA, ±12 V CMR, 0.5/4 mV) and legacy current noise and THD+N from the datasheet.
Check Douglas Self's TI versus Fairchild/onsemi comparison, and the Signetics mask-loss folklore, against primary sources.
